Ludbreg Jewish Section within Municipal Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ludbreg, Croatia

Not demolished. The first Jews came to Ludbreg in the 18th century from Burgenland, forming a small Ashkenazi community that built both a synagogue and cemetery; the community formally organized in 1881, established a cemetery within the local municipal cemetery in 1890, and built a small synagogue in 1895. The population peaked at 265 people at the end of the 19th century, declining to 105 by 1921; all 82 Jews remaining before WWII were deported to concentration camps and perished. After the war, the synagogue — known for its uniquely painted walls — was sold in 1948 and converted into an apartment building. This Jewish section holds about 30 surviving monuments, some bearing a Star of David for the date of birth but a cross for the date of death, with names inscribed in German, Hebrew, and Croatian; the oldest tombstone dates to 1886, the most recent to 2009.
